sections.preamble: You are an expert coding assistant operating inside pi, a coding agent harness. You help users by reading files, executing commands, editing code, and writing new files.
sections.tools:
<tools>
- read: Read file contents
- bash: Execute bash commands (ls, grep, find, etc.)
- edit: Make precise file edits with exact text replacement, including multiple disjoint edits in one call
- write: Create or overwrite files
- commit_amend: Stage all changes and amend the last commit without changing its message.
- commit_changes: Run git commit with staged changes using a conventional commit message. If pre-commit hooks fail, fix and retry.
- batch_create_para_docs: Batch-create multiple PARA docs with auto-linking, validating atomicity and following citation conventions
- ask: Deterministic research pipeline — KB-first, sufficiency-gated cycles, knowledge base write-back
- expand_bullet_points: Search reputable web sources and expand unclear bullet points into coherent ideas
- batch_extract_failed: Batch-extract URLs that failed Obscura+HTTP extraction. Uses Tavily extract API.
- fetch_url: Fetch a URL and get its content as Markdown
- search_para_docs: Search for relevant knowledge documents in Areas, Projects, Resources directories
- create_para_doc: Create a new knowledge document in the PARA directory structure — validates atomicity, uses Pandoc citations
- update_para_doc: Update and renew frontmatter of an existing knowledge document
- list_para_tags: List all existing unique tags in the PARA knowledge base
- find_existing_summary: Check if a URL already has a saved summary before re-summarising
- resolve_citation: Resolve a citation source: parse via citation.js, check dedup, insert into notes.db and append to ref.bib if new.
- research_engine: Full research pipeline — KB-first deterministic cycles, knowledge base write-back, synthesized answer
- web_search: Search the web (3-phase: SearXNG academic -> filtered -> general, then Tavily, then Bing RSS). Use tier=1 for academic, tier=2 for filtered web (default site:edu|gov), tier=3 for general. Pass category='it' for tech/software, 'news' for news queries, etc.
- validate_frontmatter: Scan and validate YAML frontmatter of PARA documents
- standardize_frontmatter: Batch standardise frontmatter field names across all PARA documents
- check_frontmatter: Check a specific PARA document's YAML frontmatter for issues

In addition to the tools above, you may have access to other custom tools depending on the project.
</tools>
sections.rules:
<rules>
- Use bash for file operations like ls, rg, find
- Use read to examine files instead of cat or sed.
- You can inspect PI_* environment variables for current model and session details.
- Use edit for precise changes (edits[].oldText must match exactly)
- When changing multiple separate locations in one file, use one edit call with multiple entries in edits[] instead of multiple edit calls
- Each edits[].oldText is matched against the original file, not after earlier edits are applied. Do not emit overlapping or nested edits. Merge nearby changes into one edit.
- Keep edits[].oldText as small as possible while still being unique in the file. Do not pad with large unchanged regions.
- Use write only for new files or complete rewrites.
- Use commit_amend after archiving a completed plan file to include the archived file in the implementation commit.
- Use commit_changes to finalize a commit after generating the message. If pre-commit hooks fail, fix the issues and call commit_changes again.
- Do NOT use commit_amend as a fallback for commit_changes failures — commit_amend rewrites history and violates hash continuity.
- If git commands are blocked by the sandbox, ask the user to run them outside the sandbox (e.g., 'Please run: git rm <file>'), then retry.
- Use batch_create_para_docs when creating 3+ related documents to save tool calls and enable batch auto-linking.
- Each document in the array has: title, content, tags, area (Resources/Projects/Areas), optional description, optional source.
- After creation, the tool auto-links all documents in the batch to each other using BM25 semantic similarity.
- Follow PARA conventions: Resources for reference/theory, Areas for responsibilities, Projects for practical work.
- Use Pandoc-style citations (@citekey / [@citekey]) referencing @ref.bib for any sourced claims.
- Apply atomic principle: one key idea per document (one research question + one indicative answer), keep concise.
- Each document is validated for atomicity before creation; violating documents are rejected individually.
- Citations are validated: all @citekey references must exist in notes.db. If any doc has unresolved citations, the entire batch is rejected.
- Call ask first when you need supporting information — it researches the knowledge base and web, then improves the knowledge base.
- Results are written to KNOWLEDGE_DIR (from .env), not the current working directory.
- Pass mode:"deep" for broad questions; results arrive as a follow-up message while you keep working.
- Pass avoidQuestions/knownSources from a previous result's digest to avoid duplicate work.
- Every result includes the digest, gaps, and the state file path for inspection.
- Use search_para_docs first when the user asks a knowledge question.
- Pass the user's question as query and infer relevant tags from context.
- Cite sources using BibTeX citation keys from @ref.bib. Use [@citekey] or @citekey inline.
- For existing PARA docs, reference by path — no BibTeX entry needed.
- Pass 1-3 focused research questions; the engine searches the knowledge base before any web search.
- The tool reports sources, answer, write-back status, and gaps — reference them in your answer.
- Be concise in your responses
- Show file paths clearly when working with files
</rules>

<project_instructions path="/home/lam/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md">
# Pi Coding Conventions

These rules apply to all code written in this environment.

## Language Use
- Casual business English
- No emojis
- Concise, precise, straightforward

## Coding Style
- Use **TypeScript** for all pi extensions and tools; otherwise, use the language as the project dictate.
- Each file must be **≤ 300 lines**. Split into modules when exceeding.
- Every exported function must have a **JSDoc comment** describing purpose, parameters, and return value.
- Use `import type` for type-only imports. Prefer `interface` over `type` for object shapes.
- Use `const` over `let` where possible. Avoid `any` — use `unknown` and narrow.

## Extension Structure
- Extensions go in `~/.pi/agent/extensions/<name>/index.ts` for global extensions and `<local-dir>/.pi/extensions/<name>/index.ts` for local extensions.
- Use the directory-with-index.ts pattern for multi-file extensions.
- Content files (templates, prompts) go in `content/` as `.md` or `.txt`, loaded at runtime via `readFile`.
- Skills go in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` with frontmatter.

## Commits
- Use conventional commits: `feat:`, `fix:`, `refactor:`, `docs:`, `chore:`, etc.
- Describe what and why, not how. Keep the subject line under 75 characters.

## Naming
- Files: `kebab-case.ts`
- Functions: `camelCase`
- Classes/types: `PascalCase`
- Constants: `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE`
- Variables: `camelCase`

</project_instructions>

<project_instructions path="/home/lam/data/professional/jobs/company/konsulin/git-repo/gateway/AGENTS.md">
# Konsulin Gateway — Agent's Guide
Federation trust root, money hub, integration hub. Go + SQLite, single-node. Never stores clinical data or plaintext PII.
PRD: `PROPOSAL.md`. Wire contract: `docs/api/` Bruno collections (normative).

## Commands
```bash
go run ./cmd/http                # dev server
go build -o gateway ./cmd/http   # production
go run ./cmd/migration           # DB migrations
docker compose up -d             # deps
mise run qc --api             # API conformance (gateway + bru)
go test ./...                    # tests
```

## Navigation
`cmd/AGENTS.md` · `internal/AGENTS.md` · `docs/AGENTS.md` · `docs/api/AGENTS.md`

## Tech Stack
Go (see `.mise.toml`) · Chi v5 · SQLite modernc.org (WAL) · Ed25519 (ES256 fallback) · Xendit · Zap · Viper · TLS-only

## Architecture
Three planes, one SQLite, one node:
1. **Registry/Resolver** — party onboarding, key management, identity hashing (GW-PARTY, GW-IDX)
2. **Money** — Xendit invoices, settlement, pricing (GW-PAY)
3. **Integration** — signed webhook delivery, retry, DLQ (GW-HOOK)
Cross-cutting: `services/sts` (tickets), `services/audit` (events), `services/admin` (operator console)

## Security Invariants
1. No payload bytes in any store (standing test)
2. No plaintext PII — `HMAC(normalized, pepper)` only
3. Pepper: never in code, DB, logs, or commits
4. Fail closed — any verification failure denies
5. TLS only — refuse non-TLS; no mTLS
6. Metadata-only audit — `(from, to, scope, jti, ts, outcome)`

## Boundaries
**Always**: run tests before commits, follow naming conventions.
**Ask first**: modify DB schema, add deps, change security paths, change Xendit callback URL.
**Never**: commit secrets/pepper, store clinical payloads, log PII, bypass TLS.

## Hook Bypass Policy

`--no-verify` is permitted:
- WIP commits pushed to a feature branch for early backup
- Commits that touch only docs (`.md`, `.toml`, `.yaml`)

`--no-verify` is never permitted:
- Commits that touch `.go` files
- Any push that skips integration tests

If CI fails and the last commit used `--no-verify`, that is a review flag.

## Testing

TDD is required for any function that directly or indirectly affects user experience or endpoint contracts. This includes handlers, services, drivers, and shared packages (JWT, hashing, identity).

- **Unit tests**: `_test.go` alongside source.
- **Integration tests**: `integration/` directory.
- **Security invariants**: distributed across packages.
- **Assertions**: use `github.com/stretchr/testify` — `require` for setup, `assert` for outcomes (see docs/TEST.md §4).

See `docs/TEST.md` for test authoring guide.

## Conventions
Clean Architecture: `delivery → services → contracts → drivers`. DB access via `drivers/sqlite` only.
Error envelope: `{error: {code, message, request_id}}`. Idempotency-Key on all creates.
JWT: `iss=gateway, aud=<recipient>, sub=<sender>, scope, purpose, jti, exp`.

</project_instructions>
</project_context>

toolsAdded.name: read
toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. For text files, output is truncated to 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Use offset/limit for large files. When you need the full file, continue with offset until complete.

path.description: Path to the file to read (relative or absolute)

offset.description: Line number to start reading from (1-indexed)

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to read

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

path.description: Path to the file to write (relative or absolute)

content.description: Content to write to the file

toolsAdded.name: commit_amend
toolsAdded.description: Auto-stage all changes then perform git commit --amend --no-edit to include them in the last commit without changing the commit message. Also runs pre-commit hooks before amending (git's --amend skips hooks by default). WARNING: This rewrites the previous commit hash. Do NOT use as a fallback for commit_changes failures. Use only after archiving completed files to include them in the implementation commit.

toolsAdded.name: commit_changes
toolsAdded.description: Run git commit with staged changes. Auto-stages all changes before committing (like commit_amend). Call this after generating a commit message. If pre-commit hooks fail, fix issues and call this tool again with the same message.

message.description: Conventional commit message (subject line, ≤75 chars, e.g. 'feat(auth): add login')

body.description: Optional body for multi-line commit messages. Use only when extra context is needed.

toolsAdded.name: batch_create_para_docs
toolsAdded.description: Create multiple PARA knowledge documents (markdown + YAML frontmatter) in one call, index all of them in notes.db, and run batch auto-linking across them. Files are written to KNOWLEDGE_DIR (from .env), not the current working directory. Each document follows: PARA classification — Resources (reference/theory), Areas (responsibilities/skills), Projects (deliverables/practical work). Atomic principle — one key idea per note (one research question + one indicative answer). Validates atomicity (single coherent topic — one research question and one indicative answer) and citation references for each doc before creation. Filenames auto-generated as kebab-case slug from title. Citations: Pandoc-style @citekey (narrative) or [@citekey] (parenthetical) from @ref.bib. Run list_para_tags first and reuse existing tags. Provide short description ≤ 200 chars for better BM25 search. Recommended body: ## Summary (2-4 paragraphs), ## Key Points, ## Sources.

description.description: Short summary ≤ 200 characters, enriches BM25 search

autoLink.description: Whether to run semantic auto-linking across the batch after creation (default: true)

toolsAdded.name: ask
toolsAdded.description: Deterministic research pipeline for a question: KB-first, then tiered web search, per-source summarization, and sufficiency-gated cycles. Writes results back to the knowledge base (KNOWLEDGE_DIR from .env, not the cwd). Quick mode runs in-tool (1 cycle, 5 sources); deep mode runs a background job and delivers via followUp.

mode.description: quick (default, in-tool) or deep (background job, followUp delivery)

avoidQuestions.description: Questions already asked in earlier runs — never repeated

toolsAdded.name: expand_bullet_points
toolsAdded.description: Expands unclear bullet points or brief ideation from a PARA knowledge document into coherent, researched paragraphs by searching reputable web sources.

docPath.description: Relative path to the PARA document containing unclear bullet points, e.g. "Projects/definition-of-resilience.md".

bullets.description: Specific bullet-point texts to expand. Omit to auto-detect all brief bullet points in the document body.

focusArea.description: Optional theme or angle to guide the expansion, e.g. 'clinical applications' or 'neuroscience research'. Helps narrow the web search.

toolsAdded.name: batch_extract_failed

toolsAdded.name: fetch_url
toolsAdded.description: Fetch a URL and get its content as Markdown.

toolsAdded.name: search_para_docs
toolsAdded.description: Search the SQLite-indexed PARA documents (Areas/Projects/Resources) by tags and content. Uses FTS5 BM25 ranking for text search with tag filtering.

toolsAdded.name: create_para_doc
toolsAdded.description: Create a new PARA knowledge document (markdown + YAML frontmatter) and index it in notes.db. Files are written to KNOWLEDGE_DIR (from .env), not the current working directory. Conventions: PARA classification — Resources for reference/theory, Areas for responsibilities/skills, Projects for deliverables/practical work. description.description: Short summary ≤ 200 characters, enriches BM25 search

toolsAdded.name: update_para_doc
toolsAdded.description: Update an existing markdown file's body content and renew its YAML frontmatter (date refreshed, author: pi / editor: lam preserved). Also syncs the SQLite index including the FTS5 term index.

description.description: Short summary ≤ 200 characters (omit to keep existing; empty string to clear)

source.description: Replacement source URL (omit to keep existing; empty string to clear)

toolsAdded.name: list_para_tags
toolsAdded.description: Return all unique tags from the SQLite-indexed PARA documents (Areas/Projects/Resources). Use this before create_para_doc to choose existing tags and avoid tag proliferation.

toolsAdded.name: find_existing_summary
toolsAdded.description: Check whether a URL already has a summary saved in the SQLite knowledge base.

url.description: The URL to check for existing summaries

content.description: Optional extracted text content for content-based similarity matching.

toolsAdded.name: resolve_citation
toolsAdded.description: Parse a URL or DOI via citation.js, generate a unique BibTeX citekey, deduplicate against the SQLite knowledge base, and append new entries to @ref.bib.

title.description: Title (needed when citation.js cannot parse the URL).

toolsAdded.name: research_engine
toolsAdded.description: Run the full research pipeline: KB-first search, tiered web search, per-source summarization, sufficiency-gated cycles, then knowledge base write-back (KNOWLEDGE_DIR from .env, not cwd). Returns sources, a synthesized answer, write-back status, and a progress digest.

questions.description: Research questions to investigate in parallel

toolsAdded.name: web_search
toolsAdded.description: Three-phase web search: SearXNG category-based search (1→2→3), then Tavily, then Bing RSS with domain filtering (Phase 3 only). Override via category: 'it' for tech/software, 'news' for news, 'web' for filtered web. Tier 3 — general category (broad exploration, blogs, any web). Fallback chain (when no tier forced): SearXNG >3 results → Tavily → Bing RSS (domain-filtered).

category.description: Override SearXNG category for the chosen tier. Useful for context-aware tier 2: 'it' for software/tech, 'news' for news, 'web' for general web. Only applied when tier is set. See @.pi/extensions/web-search/AGENTS.md for all supported categories.

toolsAdded.name: validate_frontmatter
toolsAdded.description: Scan all PARA markdown files and check for invalid YAML frontmatter.

path.description: Specific file path. Omit to scan all.

# Plan 018: Flow Harness — One Opt-in Proof of Security Behavior

**Milestone:** M5 (Security hardening)
**Depends on:** Plan 014 (Bruno conformance), Plan 015 (QC idempotency), e2e harness (`internal/app/integration/e2e`)
**ADR Refs:** ADR-011 (fail-closed), ADR-017 (idempotency)

Plans 018–022 supersede the previous T5–T19 hardening contract. This plan
comes first: every later plan adds its scenarios to the harness defined here.

## Purpose

One opt-in harness proves the gateway's security behavior over the wire,
against the published contract. Every request a scenario sends is the
`docs/api` contract file itself, run through `bru run`, so the published
reference and the security proof cannot drift apart. `docs/api` carries
only the contract. Order, state, and negative cases live in Go.

## Expectations and assessment

**Expectation:** `docs/api` stays the single source of truth and is
published for collaborators, while one command runs every scenario and
asserts best security practice.

**Current state:**

- Two drivers. `scripts/bru-run.sh` runs the whole collection as one
  `bru run`, chained through `bru.runner.setNextRequest` and
  `bru.setVar`/`getVar` (about 30 files chain, about 15 read chain state).
  The e2e suite (`internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go`) runs one
  contract file per `bru run` and carries state in Go
  (`Vars`/`Extract`/`Pre`/`Expect`).
- Fact: `setNextRequest` is a no-op in single-file runs, and `bru.setVar`
  state does not survive across runs. The e2e runner already works
  without either.
- The QC chain authenticates with a party JWT minted in shell
  (`scripts/provide-test-environment.sh`) before the party exists, with
  `iss: "qc-party"` and no `aud`. That blocks any `iss == party_id` rule
  (plan 020), and is why the previous T5 attempts stalled.
- `docs/api/AGENTS.md` documents the QC order in prose only. Flow logic
  (order, state, drill routing) lives inside the published contract.
- Two entries: `mise run qc --api` (needs a running gateway, drives
  `bru-run.sh`) and `mise run qc --e2e` (boots its own gateway).

**Best practice:** contracts describe one exchange each; a test driver owns
sequencing, state, key custody, and negative cases. Tokens are minted by
the driver after registration, with the keys held only in the driver
process, the same way a real party would.

**Sensible?** Yes. Merging the two drivers removes the duplicate state model
and lets every security plan prove its controls end to end.

## Decisions

- Flows are Go scenario tables in `internal/app/integration/`, not YAML.
  They are compile-checked, and they stay out of the published reference.
- `docs/api` is pure contract. It is published via `bru docs generate`.
  Flow manifests are never published there.
- Narrative flow guides for collaborators are hand-written in
  `docs/flows/*.md`, each step linking to its contract file.
- Party keys live in driver memory. An Ed25519 key is about 96 bytes, and
  sign/verify cost tens of microseconds (published Go benchmarks, not
  measured here). A run uses a handful of parties, so memory is not a
  constraint. The real cost is gateway-side: one indexed `kid` lookup in
  `party_keys` plus one verify per request. Load testing is out of scope.
- The QC environment may hold ephemeral test keys for the duration of a
  run. With in-memory driver keys, nothing needs exporting.
- `mise run qc --flow` is opt-in, not pre-commit. Estimated runtime is a
  few minutes (about 50 `bru` process spawns); unmeasured.

## Changes

1. **Harness package.** Move the scenario runner, gateway launcher,
   capture server, and verifiers into one harness under
   `internal/app/integration/` (keep `e2e/` or rename to `flow/`; one
   package either way). Keep the existing runner API
   (`Step{File, Vars, Extract, Pre, Expect}`, `runScenarios`). Add
   `ExpectFn` for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express.
   Behavior: existing e2e scenarios pass unchanged under the new entry.

2. **Single entry.** `scripts/qc.sh` gains `--flow`
   (`GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -run Flow -v`).
   `--api` and `--e2e` are removed; `.mise.toml` description updated.
   Harness unit tests (`scenario_test.go`, `bru_test.go`, capture verifier
   tests) keep running in `--test` without a gateway.
   Behavior: `mise run qc --flow` boots one gateway and runs every
   scenario; `mise run qc --test` needs no gateway.

3. **Driver-owned party lifecycle.** A `party` helper generates Ed25519
   (and later X25519) keys in memory, enrolls through the contract file,
   reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report, and mints
   party tokens in Go via one minter shared with the golden vectors
   (plan 020). Negative tokens (forged signature, foreign key, past
   `iat`/`exp`, wrong `typ`, wrong `aud`/`iss`) come from the same minter.
   Behavior: a scenario authenticates with a token whose `iss` equals the
   registered `party_id`.

4. **Port the QC chain.** The 28-call QC chain becomes scenario
   `FlowQCChain`, one step per contract file in the documented order.
   Values formerly passed via `bru.setVar` (`partyId`, `adminJwt`,
   `bootstrapToken`, `globalKey`, `approvalTicket`, `listingId`,
   `paymentId`, `accessToken`, `webhookId`, `listingCount`) become
   `Extract` → `Vars`. Behavior: the full chain passes with no
   `setNextRequest` involvement.

5. **Port the drill.** `scripts/bru-drill.sh` becomes scenario
   `FlowPaymentDrill` with `drillMode=1` as an input.
   `scripts/payment-capture.sh` runs it and keeps reading the
   `DRILL_PAYMENT_URL=` marker from stdout. Behavior:
   `mise run payment` works as before.

6. **docs/api becomes pure contract.** Remove `bru.runner.setNextRequest`
   and chain `bru.setVar`/`getVar` from every `.yml`. Cross-request
   assertions (`list-parties`, `party-detail`, `audit-events`,
   `get-listings`, `resolve-identity`, `mint-approval`) take the prior
   value as a declared input or move to `ExpectFn`. Runtime values move
   from `{{process.env.x}}` to `{{x}}`; static config may stay
   `process.env`. `drillMode` stays an input. Rewrite the Chaining and
   QC Chain sections of `docs/api/AGENTS.md` to describe inputs and point
   to `docs/flows/`. Behavior: `bru docs generate` output contains no
   chain logic; every file runs standalone with declared inputs.

7. **Retire shell drivers.** Delete `scripts/bru-run.sh`. Remove JWT
   minting and party key generation from
   `scripts/provide-test-environment.sh` (it keeps gateway env only).
   Remove `scripts/bru-drill.sh` once task 5 lands.

8. **Route auth matrix.** Each contract `.yml` declares its auth class in
   `info.tags` (`auth:admin`, `auth:party`, `auth:ticket`,
   `auth:provider`, `auth:public`). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists
   every file and asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public
   route. Behavior: a new authenticated route without a marker fails the
   matrix; a marked route that answers without a credential fails it.

9. **Standing tests join the entry.** Existing e2e scenarios
   (marketplace multi-party, invocation result loop, access-token
   negatives, forged callback, result auth-mode switch) and integration
   standing tests (`payload_bytes_test.go`, `plaintext_pii_test.go`,
   `ticket_verification_test.go`) run under `--flow`.

10. **Narrative guides.** `docs/flows/onboarding.md`,
    `docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md`,
    `docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md`, `docs/flows/payment.md`: prose
    sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to
    its `docs/api` file. Hand-written; updated by the plan that changes
    the flow.

### Shared security-assessment format (plans 019–022)

Every plan lists its flow scenarios in one table:

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| Scenario | Observable over-the-wire case the harness runs |
| Threat | What an attacker or faulty party tries |
| Control (best practice) | The control that should stop it |
| Current status | What the code does today (met / partial / missing) |
| Gap → task | The plan task that closes the gap, or "—" when met |

Each scenario becomes one `Flow*` scenario or one step in a scenario. A
scenario is done only when it passes under `mise run qc --flow`.

## Flow scenarios and security assessment

| Scenario | Threat | Control (best practice) | Current status | Gap → task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| QC chain ported (28 calls) | Contract drifts from behavior | Every call runs the published file | Met via `bru-run.sh` chain | Move to driver → 4 |
| Payment drill ported | Drill breaks silently | Drill is a scenario; marker kept | Met via `bru-drill.sh` | → 5 |
| Party token minted after registration | Pre-minted token with fake `iss` hides auth bugs | Driver mints with server-assigned `party_id` | Missing (shell, `iss=qc-party`) | → 3, 7 |
| Driver-minted negative tokens | Negative paths never exercised | One minter produces forged/expired/wrong-claim tokens | Partial (e2e only) | → 3 |
| Route auth matrix | New route ships without auth | 401 without credential, derived from contract markers | Missing | → 8 |
| Contract has no chain logic | Published docs encode test flow | Inputs only; flows in Go | Missing | → 6 |
| Standing tests under one entry | Security tests skipped (not run by `--api`) | One opt-in entry runs all | Partial (split `--api`/`--e2e`) | → 2, 9 |
| TLS at Traefik edge | Plaintext traffic | Edge TLS (ADR-010) | Not testable here | — |
| Backend SDK verifier | Recipient accepts bad tickets | SDK verifies against golden vectors | Not testable here (plan 020/022) | — |

## Definition of Done

- [ ] `mise run qc --flow` boots one gateway and runs every scenario; it
      replaces `--api` and `--e2e`.
- [ ] `mise run qc --test` runs harness unit tests without a gateway.
- [ ] QC chain and payment drill pass as Go scenarios; `mise run payment`
      still prints `DRILL_PAYMENT_URL`.
- [ ] No `setNextRequest` or chain `bru.setVar`/`getVar` remains in
      `docs/api`; `docs/api/AGENTS.md` describes inputs.
- [ ] `scripts/bru-run.sh` and `scripts/bru-drill.sh` deleted; no JWT
      minting in shell.
- [ ] Party tokens are minted in Go after registration.
- [ ] Route auth matrix passes and covers every non-public contract.
- [ ] `docs/flows/` guides exist for onboarding, approval, delivery,
      payment.
- [ ] `go test ./...` green.

## Out of scope

- Gateway behavior changes (plans 019–022).
- Load or capacity testing of the gateway.
- TLS at the Traefik edge and the backend SDK verifier.
- An OpenAPI spec (Bruno stays normative).

content.text:
## Summary
There are two test layers. `internal/app/integration/` (package `integration`) holds security tests that always run against a real in-process service stack. `internal/app/integration/e2e/` (package `e2e`) boots a real gateway binary, drives it with `bru run` over `docs/api`, and only runs when `GATEWAY_E2E=1` is set at runtime; the repo has no build tags anywhere. JWTs are minted in two separate places: the shell script `scripts/provide-test-environment.sh` (openssl, EdDSA) for the Bruno chain, and Go code (`sts.Mint`, `webhooks.Signer`, the e2e `partyFixture.mintJWT`) using `golang-jwt/jwt/v5`. Committed golden vectors live in `testdata/golden/`.

## Key Files

**e2e harness (package `e2e`)**
- `internal/app/integration/e2e/harness.go` — gateway lifecycle and the gate:
  - `e2eEnvVar = "GATEWAY_E2E"` (:28); `e2eEnabled()` (:54-56) checks `== "1"`.
  - `suiteGateway(t)` (:60-64) calls `t.Skipf` unless enabled, otherwise boots the gateway once via `sync.Once`.
  - `launchGateway()` (:82-160) runs `exec.Command(binPath)` with `Dir = tmp` (so a repo `.env` can't leak in), a free port and a temp data dir, then polls `/health`.
  - `buildGateway` (:243-254) runs `go build -o binPath ./cmd/http` from the repo root.
  - Other helpers: `waitHealthy` (:180), `stop` (:206), `shutdownSuite` (:74).
- `e2e/harness_test.go` — `TestMain` (:18) runs the tests then calls `shutdownSuite()`. Also `TestE2EGate`, `TestSuiteGatewayHealthy`, `TestGatewayTeardown`.
- `e2e/scenario.go` — table-driven runner:
  - `Expect{Status int; ErrorCode string}` (:38-41).
  - `Step` (:43-56):
    ```go
    type Step struct {
        Name    string
        File    string            // relative to docs/api
        Vars    map[string]string // --env-var pairs; may reference {{var}}
        Extract map[string]string // var name -> JSON path
        Expect  Expect
        Pre     func(vars map[string]string) error
    }
    ```
  - `Scenario{Name string; Steps []Step}` (:60-63).
  - `func runScenarios(t *testing.T, scenarios []Scenario)` (:71) runs each scenario as a subtest and fails on the first mismatch. `runScenario` is at :88.
- `e2e/bru.go` — `runBru` (:69) runs `exec.CommandContext(ctx, "bru", ...)` with a 60s timeout. `parseBruReport` (:109) and `actualResponse` (:126) parse the JSON report and discard bru's embedded assertion verdicts, so all assertions happen on the Go side.
- `e2e/capture.go` — capture server:
  - `captureServer` (:51-63); `newCaptureServer(t, jwksURL)` (:65-80) builds an `httptest.NewServer(mux)` (:77).
  - Routes `/engine` (`handleEngine` :92, `engineURL()` :82) and `/buyer-callbacks` (`handleCallbacks` :112, `callbacksURL()` :86).
  - Records into channels with capacity 8; `waitForInvocation` (:146), `waitForResult` (:162).
- `e2e/capture_verify.go` — `deliveryVerifier` (:26) verifies the gateway-signed bearer on each capture against the live JWKS (fetched once, cached). It denies on signature, kid, issuer, purpose or expiry failure.
- `e2e/fixtures.go` — per-run Ed25519 party keys:
  - `partyFixture` (:31) with `mintJWT` (:62), which uses `jwt.NewWithClaims(&jwt.SigningMethodEd25519{}, …)`.
  - Admin helpers: `adminLogin` (:80), `createBootstrapToken` (:94), `registerParty` (:108), `promoteParty` (:132).
- `e2e/scenarios_marketplace_test.go` — `TestMarketplaceMultiPartyChain` (plan 016).
- `e2e/scenarios_invocation_test.go` — `TestInvocationResultLoop` (plan 017).
- `e2e/scenarios_payments_test.go` — `TestAccessTokenNegatives`, `TestForgedCallbackScenario`, plus DB surgery helpers `mutateGatewayDB` (:276) and `setPaymentStatus` (:258).
- Unit tests for the harness pieces: `e2e/bru_test.go`, `e2e/capture_test.go`, `e2e/fixtures_test.go`, and `e2e/scenario_test.go` (uses the `stubRequestExec` seam).
- `e2e/result_switch_test.go` — runs `exec.Command("bru")` (:76) and calls `t.Skip("bru CLI not on PATH")` (:32). This file was **not** in the scout's directory inventory; its purpose was not described.

**Always-on integration tests (package `integration`)**
- `internal/app/integration/harness_test.go` — temp-file SQLite plus real crypto, repos and services; provides `newHarness`, `makeActiveParty`, `makeFreeListing`.
- `payload_bytes_test.go` (T1), `plaintext_pii_test.go` (T2), `ticket_verification_test.go` (T3–T6):
  - All three are `package integration` (internal, not `_test`).
  - None has build tags, env gating, `testing.Short()` or `t.Skip`; they run on plain `go test ./...`.
  - Scouts disagree on line numbers for these tests (e.g. `TestNoPlaintextPIIAtRest` at :53 vs :47; `TestRevokedKeyFailsVerification` at :75 vs :67). Re-check before citing.

**Scripts and config**
- `scripts/qc.sh` — flags are order-independent; an unknown flag exits 1. With no flags it runs everything **except** `--api` and `--e2e`. Scope comes from `QC_SCOPE`, otherwise it is `staged` under lefthook and `all` in CI.
  - `--test` runs `go test ./...`.
  - `--api` runs `bash scripts/gateway.sh --run bash scripts/bru-run.sh`.
  - `--e2e` runs `GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/e2e/... -v` (:113).
- `.mise.toml`:
  - `[tasks.qc] run = "bash scripts/qc.sh"`; the env var is not set here.
  - Other tasks: `gateway`, `payment` (→ `scripts/payment-capture.sh`), `docs` (`bru docs generate`).
  - There are no `test`, `e2e` or `bru` tasks. `bru-drill.sh` is not wired to any task.
  - Pinned tool: `npm:@usebruno/cli = 4.2.1`.
- `scripts/gateway.sh` — reached through `qc --api`; this file was not read directly, and its details come from the qc.sh scout. In `--run` mode it:
  - deletes and rebuilds `./gateway`;
  - uses a fresh `mktemp` `APP_DB_PATH` and a random `APP_PORT`;
  - sets fast webhook polling/backoff (1s) and `APP_RATE_LIMIT_MAX=1000`;
  - evals `provide-test-environment.sh` for credentials;
  - stops the gateway via an EXIT trap.
- `scripts/bru-run.sh` — `cd docs/api && bru run --bail` with camelCased `--env-var` values (`gatewayUrl`, `partyJwt`, `partyPublicKey`, `partyKid`, `operatorUsername`, …). It does not set `drillMode`.
- `scripts/bru-drill.sh` — same chain with `drillMode=1`, ending at Create Payment. It exports `gatewayUrl` as a real process env var and prints `DRILL_PAYMENT_URL=`.
- `scripts/payment-capture.sh` — Xendit sandbox harness:
  - requires the real `APP_XENDIT_TOKEN` / `APP_XENDIT_CALLBACK_TOKEN`;
  - starts the gateway with `gateway.sh --bg`, mounts a Tailscale funnel, and runs `bru-drill.sh`;
  - polls the audit table via `python3`/sqlite for up to `DEADLINE_SECONDS` (default 600);
  - mints no JWTs itself.
- `scripts/provide-test-environment.sh` — the only shell JWT minter; it outputs eval-able `export` lines (or writes `.env` with `--write-env`).
  - **Algorithm:** EdDSA with header `{"alg":"EdDSA","kid":"qc-party-kid-1"}` (L61).
  - **Key:** a fresh `openssl genpkey -algorithm ed25519` key (L32-33). `PARTY_PUBLIC_KEY` is the raw last 32 bytes of the SPKI DER (L59).
  - **Claims:** only `{"iss":"qc-party","iat","exp"}` with `exp = iat + 300` (L62-63); no `sub` or `aud`.
  - **Signing:** `openssl pkeyutl -sign -rawin` (L73-79), with a 64-byte signature check.
  - It also generates a rotated keypair (`qc-party-kid-2`, public key only), gateway/admin signing keys, and a bcrypt operator credential.

**Go JWT and golden infrastructure**
- `go.mod` — the only JWT library is `github.com/golang-jwt/jwt/v5 v5.3.1`.
- `internal/app/services/sts/mint.go` — mints approval/access tickets:
  - `func Mint(priv ed25519.PrivateKey, req Request) (*Ticket, error)`.
  - Claims: `iss=gateway`, `aud`, `sub`, `scope`, `purpose`, `researcher_hash`, `jti`, `iat`, `exp`. TTL is capped at 15 minutes.
  - `kid` is the RFC 7638 thumbprint; `typ` is set per ticket type.
- `internal/app/services/sts/verify.go` — `Verify(pub, token, expectedAud)`.
- `internal/app/services/webhooks/signer.go` — `NewSigner(priv)` with methods `DeliveryJWT`, `EventJWT`, `EventJWTAt` (fixed iat/exp, used for golden vectors), `ResultTicket`, `ResultTicketWithJTI`, `VerifyResultTicket`.
- `internal/app/services/admin/auth.go` — `signToken` is unexported; the only entry point is `Login`.
- `pkg/keys/` — `ParseEd25519PrivateKey`/`ParseEd25519PublicKey` (`ed25519.go`), `JWKThumbprint`, `Ed25519JWK`, `ES256JWK` (`jwks.go`), plus `es256.go`.
- `pkg/jwttyp/jwttyp.go` — `typ` constants and `Require`.
- `cmd/genkey/main.go` — generates keys only. No cmd tool mints JWTs.
- `testdata/golden/` — committed test-only signing key, `gateway-jwks.json`, four `settlement-{paid,expired}-{buyer,provider}.json` vectors in `{name, claims, jwt}` format, and a `README.md`. There are no `*.golden`, `*.jwt` or `vectors*.json` files.
- `internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go`:
  - checks the vectors byte-for-byte at a fixed `2026-01-01T00:00:00Z` with TTL 900s;
  - pins the JWKS kid;
  - `TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey` fails if non-test code references `testdata/golden`;
  - vectors are regenerated with `-update`.

**docs/api Bruno collection**
- `docs/api/*.yml` — 41 files in total.

| Pattern | Files | Occurrences |
|---|---|---|
| `setNextRequest` | 30 | 33 |
| `bru.setVar` | 10 | 11 |
| `bru.getVar` | 6 | 6 |
| `process.env` | 30 | 74 |

- The files form one linear QC chain: `meta/health.yml` → … → `admin/revoke-party.yml`, which ends with `setNextRequest(null)`.
- Branch points: `payments/create-payment.yml` stops early in drill mode; `admin/promote-party.yml` reads `drillMode` via `bru.getEnvVar`.
- Heaviest `process.env` users: `parties/register-party.yml` (9) and `payments/create-listing.yml` (6).

## Architecture Insights
- **Gating is runtime only.** `e2e` tests skip through `suiteGateway(t)` unless `GATEWAY_E2E=1`, so `go test ./...` stays fast. The env var is set by `qc.sh --e2e`, `.github/workflows/pr-check.yml:49` and `.github/workflows/e2e-nightly.yml:19`. There is no Makefile.
- **The Go harness runs single requests, not chains.** `runBru` executes one `docs/api` request file at a time. The Go `Step` table replaces the yml `setNextRequest`/`bru.setVar` chaining with `Vars`, `Extract` and `{{var}}` interpolation, and ignores bru's own assertions. The 33 `setNextRequest` and 17 `setVar`/`getVar` usages encode the same chain logic that a flow harness would need to reproduce or bypass.
- **Two parallel credential paths exist.**
  - Shell path: `provide-test-environment.sh` → `gateway.sh` → `bru-run.sh`/`bru-drill.sh` → `{{process.env.*}}`.
  - Go path: `fixtures.go` (`mintJWT`, admin login/register/promote) passes `--env-var` values directly to an isolated gateway.
  - A Go flow harness can reuse `fixtures.go`, `sts.Mint`, or `webhooks.Signer` with keys from `keys.ParseEd25519PrivateKey`.
- **Isolation pattern:** a temp working directory, temp DB, free port and per-run keys apply in both the Go launcher and `gateway.sh`.

## Suggestions
- Read `e2e/result_switch_test.go` (purpose unknown) and `scripts/gateway.sh` (only described second-hand).
- Confirm the exact test line numbers in `plaintext_pii_test.go` and `ticket_verification_test.go`, where scouts disagreed.
- The complete list of the 10 `bru.setVar` files was not enumerated; only 6 were named.
- Check how `scenario.go` interpolation/extraction (around `runScenario` :88) handles requests that call `setNextRequest`. A single-request `bru run` may still execute those scripts.
- Review `testdata/golden/README.md` before adding new vectors; it describes the lockstep with the `gatewayclient` SDK in the konsulin-api repo.

I've read the plan and the current harness. Here's how I'd implement it, plus a few decisions I need from you first.

## What already exists
- `internal/app/integration/e2e/` already has most of the harness:
  - **Runner:** `Step`, `runScenarios`, and `runBru`, which runs one file per `bru run`.
  - **Launcher:** `harness.go`, gated by `GATEWAY_E2E=1`.
  - **Capture server and verifier**, plus party fixtures in `fixtures.go`. `mintJWT` already mints party tokens with Ed25519.
- `runBru` already passes `Vars` both as `--env-var` and as the child's process environment. So `{{x}}` and `{{process.env.x}}` both resolve today. That means step 6 is cleanup, not a blocker.
- `info.tags` already exists in the `.yml` files (for example `tags: [parties, registration]`), so the `auth:*` markers fit the existing format.
- **CI:** `pr-check.yml` runs `qc --api` and `GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/e2e/...`. `e2e-nightly.yml` runs the same `go test` command. Both need updating.

## Proposed order (each step is one commit and stays green)
1. **Rename `e2e/` to `flow/`** and add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step`. Rename the scenario tests to `TestFlow*` so `-run Flow` picks them up. Existing scenarios must pass unchanged.
2. **Party helper and shared minter.** Move `partyFixture.mintJWT` into a small minter. It mints after registration with `iss = party_id` from the bru report (`Extract`), and has options for negative tokens: forged signature, foreign key, past `iat`/`exp`, wrong `typ`, wrong `aud`, wrong `iss`. I'd keep it test-only, under `flow/`, until plan 020 needs it for golden vectors.
3. **`FlowQCChain`:** 28 steps in the order from `docs/api/AGENTS.md`, using `Extract` and `Vars` for the 10 chain values. It runs alongside `bru-run.sh` for now; the `setNextRequest` scripts are no-ops in single-file runs.
4. **`FlowPaymentDrill`**, then switch `payment-capture.sh` to use it (see Q3).
5. **Atomic cutover:**
   - strip `setNextRequest`, `setVar` and `getVar` from `docs/api`, and move cross-request checks to inputs or `ExpectFn`;
   - convert runtime `process.env.x` to `{{x}}`;
   - delete `bru-run.sh` and `bru-drill.sh`, and remove the JWT and party-key code from `provide-test-environment.sh`;
   - replace `--api`/`--e2e` with `--flow` in `qc.sh`, `.mise.toml` and both workflows;
   - rewrite the Chaining section of `docs/api/AGENTS.md`.

   This has to be one commit, because stripping the chain logic breaks `bru-run.sh`.
6. **`FlowRouteAuthMatrix`:** add `auth:*` tags to all 41 files. The scenario walks `docs/api` and runs each non-public file with no credential, expecting 401. It fails if any file has no auth tag.
7. **Standing tests** (see Q2).
8. **`docs/flows/*.md`**, the four guides. Docs only.

## Questions
1. **Package name:** rename to `flow/`, or keep `e2e/`? Renaming touches CI and every scenario file. Keeping it is cheaper, but `qc --flow` then runs a package called `e2e`.
2. **Standing tests:** `payload_bytes_test.go`, `plaintext_pii_test.go` and `ticket_verification_test.go` are in `package integration`, aren't gated, and already run in `go test ./...`. With `-run Flow` they would be filtered out. My suggestion: `--flow` runs `./internal/app/integration/...` without a `-run` filter, so standing tests run both in `--test` and `--flow`, and the gateway-backed tests stay gated by `GATEWAY_E2E`. Is that OK, or do you want them gateway-backed too?
3. **Drill against an external gateway:** `payment-capture.sh` starts its own gateway with real Xendit tokens and a Tailscale funnel. The Go harness always launches its own. I'd add `FLOW_GATEWAY_URL` and admin-credential env vars so the harness skips `launchGateway` and targets the given URL. That means `provide-test-environment.sh` keeps producing operator credentials and gateway keys, just not party JWTs. Agreed?
4. **CI:** should `pr-check.yml` run `mise run qc --flow`, which replaces both the `--api` and `e2e` jobs? The plan says opt-in and not pre-commit, but it doesn't say anything about CI.
5. **Golden vectors:** the plan says the minter is "shared with the golden vectors (plan 020)". Is a test-only minter enough for now, with the move to `pkg/` deferred to 020?

Once you've answered these I'll tighten the plan into a final strategy.

# Plan 020: Party Authentication and Key Management

**Milestone:** M5 (Security hardening)
**Depends on:** Plan 018 (flow harness, Go minter); Plan 019 (enrollment uses `ks-party+jwt`)
**ADR Refs:** ADR-004 (Ed25519 with ES256 fallback), ADR-006 (short-lived JWT tickets), ADR-011 (fail-closed)

Supersedes old T5 (party token claims), T10 (gateway key rotation), T15
(encryption key distribution), and T18 (golden vectors) of the previous
T5–T19 contract. Resumes the stashed partial T5 work (`git stash list`:
`t5-partyauth`).

## Purpose

Every request a party sends is provably from that party, now, to this
gateway, exactly once. Every token the federation passes around has one
explicit kind, a normative claim set, and a golden vector, so the gateway
and the backend SDK cannot disagree on what is valid. Keys rotate without
breaking in-flight verification.

## Expectations and assessment

### E3. Every transaction authenticates the requestor

**Current state:**

- `PartyAuth` (`pkg/middleware/partyauth.go`) resolves the key by `kid`,
  cross-checks the stored algorithm, verifies the signature, requires
  `exp` with a 1-minute leeway (`partyauth.go:28`), and requires the party
  to be `active`.
- It does not check `iss`, `aud`, `iat`, `typ`, `jti`, or a maximum
  lifetime. A party can mint a year-long bearer token, and a captured
  token replays until it expires.
- Gateway-minted tokens already carry explicit `typ` (07205da) and
  approval/result tickets carry single-use `jti`.

**Best practice:** explicit typing (RFC 8725 §3.11), audience and issuer
binding, short lifetime, and one-time use for request tokens.

**Sensible?** Yes.

### E4. Unique key pairs per transaction

**Assessment:** literal per-transaction signing key pairs are not sensible.
A recipient can only trust a key it can look up, so each key would need
registering, and a stream of throwaway keys removes accountability: there
is no stable identity to audit or revoke.

**Restated expectation (adopted):**

- **Stable identity key per party**, rotated with a grace window.
- **Unique credential per transaction:** unique `jti`, short-lived,
  audience-bound, and body-bound (`body_sha256`, plan 022).
- **Unique encryption key per message:** JWE ECDH-ES with an ephemeral
  X25519 key per message (plan 022), against the recipient's published
  encryption key (task 4 here).

## Decisions

- Party tokens get `typ: ks-party+jwt`, matching the five gateway kinds.
- `jti` replay store for party tokens now (reverses the earlier "accept
  replay within 5 minutes").
- `iss` is the server-assigned `party_id`; `aud` is the literal `gateway`.
- Clock skew tolerance is 60 seconds.
- Golden vectors are Ed25519 only (deterministic); ES256 stays in unit
  tests.

## Changes

1. **Party token claims.** `pkg/middleware/partyauth.go`, `pkg/jwttyp`
   (add `PartyTyp = "ks-party+jwt"`). `VerifyPartyToken` requires:
   header `typ` = `ks-party+jwt`; `iss` = the `party_id` owning the `kid`;
   `aud` = `gateway`; `iat` present and ≤ now + 60s; `exp − iat` ≤ 300s;
   `jti` present. Resume stash `t5-partyauth`. The flow driver's minter
   (plan 018 task 3) emits compliant tokens. Behavior: each missing or
   wrong claim → 401.

2. **`jti` replay store.** New `party_token_jtis (party_id, jti, exp)`
   table via `drivers/sqlite`, unique on `(party_id, jti)`, inserted after
   signature and claim checks; a conflict → 401. Janitor purges rows past
   `exp` (same loop shape as the audit janitor). SQLite-backed so a
   restart does not reopen the replay window. Behavior: the same token
   twice → second is 401.

3. **Normative claim spec.** `docs/api/AGENTS.md` gets a Token Kinds
   section, one row per kind:

   | `typ` | Signer | Required claims | Verifier |
   |---|---|---|---|
   | `ks-party+jwt` | party key | iss=party_id, aud=gateway, iat, exp (≤300s), jti | gateway |
   | `ks-approval+jwt` | gateway | iss=gateway, aud, sub, scope, purpose, researcher_hash, jti, iat, exp (≤900s) | recipient party |
   | `ks-access+jwt` | gateway | iss=gateway, aud=provider, sub=buyer, scope=listing:*, purpose, jti, iat, exp | provider |
   | `ks-delivery+jwt` | gateway | iss=gateway, aud, sub, webhook_id, body_sha256, iat, exp | recipient endpoint |
   | `ks-event+jwt` | gateway | iss=gateway, aud, sub=gateway, purpose, webhook_id, body_sha256, iat, exp | party callbacks |
   | `ks-result+jwt` | gateway | iss=gateway, aud, sub, webhook_id, jti, iat, exp | gateway (single use) |

   `body_sha256` lands with plan 022; until then the spec marks it
   "required from plan 022". Plus rules: exact `typ` match, `kid` from the
   JWT header only, keys from JWKS, 60s skew, fail closed. Each contract `.yml` that carries a token
   links to its row.

4. **Encryption key publication.** `pkg/keys/x25519.go` validates a base64
   raw 32-byte X25519 key. Enrollment (plan 019 task 7) and rotation
   (`POST /v1/parties/{id}/keys`) accept optional `enc_public_key`, stored
   on the `party_keys` row (nullable column). `/v1/parties/{id}/jwks`
   emits `{kty:OKP, crv:X25519, use:enc, kid, x}` beside the sig key, with
   the same grace window. Invalid length → 400 `invalid_public_key`.

5. **Party key rotation.** Existing rotation and grace window stay; add the
   grace-expiry case to the flow (old `kid` accepted inside
   `APP_KEY_GRACE_WINDOW`, 401 after).

6. **Gateway key rotation.** `APP_GATEWAY_SIGNING_KEY_PREVIOUS` (optional,
   base64 Ed25519 public key). `/.well-known/jwks` lists current and
   previous, each `kid` its RFC 7638 thumbprint. `sts/verify.go` and
   `Signer.VerifyResultTicket` select the key by `kid` and accept the
   previous one; minting always uses the current key. Runbook in
   `docs/api/AGENTS.md`: set previous, swap current, drop previous after
   2× the longest token TTL.

7. **Golden vectors.** `testdata/golden/` gains vectors for
   `ks-delivery`, `ks-event` (service-result), `ks-approval`, `ks-access`,
   `ks-result`, and `ks-party` (signed by a committed
   `testonly-party-private.key`, verified gateway-side). `golden_test.go`
   asserts byte equality for gateway-signed vectors and acceptance of the
   party vector. README lists every vector and the coordinated
   regeneration rule (`-update`, then mirror to `../backend`).
   `TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey` stays green.

## Flow scenarios and security assessment

| Scenario | Threat | Control (best practice) | Current status | Gap → task |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Valid party token | — | All claims checked, 200 | Met (weaker check) | → 1 |
| Missing `iat` | Unbounded token | `iat` required | Missing | → 1 |
| Wrong `aud` | Token for another audience replayed here | `aud` = gateway | Missing | → 1 |
| Wrong `iss` | Key holder impersonates another party id | `iss` = party owning `kid` | Missing | → 1 |
| Lifetime > 300s | Long-lived bearer token | `exp − iat` ≤ 300s | Missing | → 1 |
| Future `iat` | Pre-dated token extends lifetime | `iat` ≤ now + 60s | Missing | → 1 |
| Expired | Stale token reuse | `exp` with 60s skew | Met | — |
| Missing or wrong `typ` | Another token kind presented as party auth | Exact `ks-party+jwt` | Missing | → 1 |
| Unknown `kid` | Forged key reference | Fail closed, 401 | Met | — |
| Foreign key signature | Signature by a non-registered key | Verify with stored key only | Met | — |
| Replayed `jti` | Captured request replayed | `jti` store until `exp` | Missing | → 2 |
| Rotation grace accept then reject | Rotation breaks traffic, or old key lives forever | Grace window, then 401 | Partial (accept tested, expiry not) | → 5 |
| Party JWKS sig + enc | Sender cannot find recipient's encryption key | X25519 `use:enc` in party JWKS | Missing | → 4 |
| Gateway JWKS current + previous | Rotation breaks in-flight verification | Two keys during rotation | Missing (single key) | → 6 |
| Previous-key verification | Ticket signed before rotation rejected | Select by `kid` | Missing | → 6 |
| Golden vectors byte-equal | Gateway and SDK drift | Committed vectors per kind | Partial (settlement only) | → 7 |

## Definition of Done

- [ ] Every scenario above passes under `mise run qc --flow` (plan 018).
- [ ] `go test ./...` green, including `TestGolden*`.
- [ ] Token Kinds spec in `docs/api/AGENTS.md` is normative and linked
      from each token-carrying contract.
- [ ] Golden vectors cover all six kinds; README updated.
- [ ] Gateway rotation runbook documented.

## Out of scope

- JWE envelope and `body_sha256` (plan 022).
- Capabilities and authorization (plan 021).
- Hardware-backed or remote key custody for parties.
- Automated gateway key rotation (stays manual).

Answering Q5 (minter ownership) with best practice, then the final plan.

## Q5: Best practice for minter ownership — keep them separate

Two minters, each next to what it proves. Sharing one would be the wrong call:

- **Golden vectors (test-side minter):** the committed `webhooks/golden_test.go` is the owner. It pins fixed timestamps and asserts byte-equality, so it must keep its own signing path (`signer.EventJWTAt` / `Signer` with `testdata/golden`). It also has the standing guard `TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey` that fails if non-test code touches `testdata/golden`. Plan 020 task 7 extends it with a committed `testonly-party-private.key` for the `ks-party` vector — still inside `golden_test.go`, still byte-pinned.
- **Flow harness (driver minter):** lives in `internal/app/integration/e2e/` next to `partyFixture`, freshly generates a key per run, and mints with *live* `iat`/`exp`/`jti`. Fixed golden timestamps and live-flow time cannot be the same code path, so the two must not merge.

The one real overlap — token claim/`typ` shapes (plan 020 task 1, `pkg/jwttyp`, `pkg/middleware`) — is already owned by production code. Both minters consume those constants; neither invents claims. That's the correct shared surface.

So: **no new `pkg/` minter, no shared package now.** The e2e minter stays test-side. When plan 020 adds the `ks-party` golden vector, it mints with the committed party key inside `golden_test.go` and asserts gateway acceptance — a third surface, but still test-side. Promote to a shared helper only if a production code path ever needs to mint party tokens (none exists today).

## Final implementation strategy (all answers folded in)

**Keep the `e2e` package.** All edits are inside `internal/app/integration/e2e/` plus scripts, `docs/api`, and CI. No rename.

Steps, each one commit, each green:

1. **`ExpectFn`** on `Step` (`scenario.go`), for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 can't express. Existing scenarios pass unchanged.
2. **Party lifecycle helper + driver minter** (`fixtures.go` minter, plan 020-compliant claims when that plan lands): generates Ed25519 in memory, enrolls via contract file, reads server `party_id` from the bru report (`Extract`), mints `iss=party_id` tokens in Go, and produces negative tokens (forged sig, foreign key, past `iat`/`exp`, wrong `typ`, wrong `aud`/`iss`). Keeps its own minter; golden vectors stay in `golden_test.go`.
3. **`FlowQCChain`** — 28 steps in documented order; the 10 chain values become `Extract`→`Vars`.
4. **`FlowPaymentDrill`** — `drillMode=1` as input; add `FLOW_GATEWAY_URL` (+ admin creds) so the harness skips `launchGateway` for an external gateway; `provide-test-environment.sh` keeps operator creds/gateway keys, drops party JWT minting.

# Finalize the Task Contract

You are drafting the atomic implementation contract from this discussion.

## Steps

1. Derive the task from the chat history. The conversation is the source of truth.
2. Draft the contract and call `save_task` with all fields.
3. `save_task` returns deterministic scan evidence and advisory warnings. Classify each evidence item (see Test classification) and revise the contract if the evidence surfaces test paths you missed. You may read files to confirm a specific fact — an exact path, an existing signature, or an `unverified` evidence item — but the discussion stays the primary source.
4. Call `save_task` again with the revised contract. Iterate until the evidence and warnings are clean or consciously accepted.

## Fields

- `title` — short task name.
- `instruction` — what to implement.
- `files` — files affected. Declare every test path the contract updates or removes here (see Test classification).
- `done` — definition of done (manual verification for non-test work).
- `behaviors[]` — each behavior: `id`, `description`, `expectedOutput`, `kind`, `status`, optional `sourceFile`.

## Co-location rule (atomic green commits)

**One behavior = test + implementation in the same commit — never split.**

- `kind: "test"` means *verified-by-test*: the behavior carries the observable outcome AND the test that verifies it. The commit lands green because test and implementation ship together.
- A behavior whose `expectedOutput` describes test artifacts only ("test file contains 3 cases", "tests covering edge cases") is invalid: such a commit is **red by construction** — a test without its implementation. Rewrite the `expectedOutput` as the observable behavior the test asserts.
- Behaviors must be **independently green-committable**: each behavior's commit passes the project's pre-commit hooks on its own. No test-before-implementation splits, no scaffold-only behaviors.
- Test updates never form their own behavior. When a behavior supersedes or removes existing tests, fold the test change into that same behavior's `instruction` and commit.

## Test classification

`save_task` returns **scan evidence**: per-`files`-entry match lines with method and confidence tags (`[symbol, high]`, `[basename, low]`, `unverified`), plus advisory warnings (`undeclared-referencing`, `declared-not-found`, `no-evidence`). Classify every evidence item:

- **preserved** — the test asserts behavior the contract keeps. Do not declare it; the guard protects it automatically.
- **superseded** — the test asserts old behavior the contract changes. Declare the path in `files`, and describe the required test update in the superseding behavior's `instruction` (folded, never its own behavior).
- **obsolete** — the test covers behavior the contract removes. Declare the path in `files`; for pure-removal contracts describe the removal in a manual behavior ("remove legacy path + its tests; suite green").
- **out-of-scope** — the test is already dead or broken for reasons unrelated to this contract. Report it to the user as a recommendation for a separate `/discuss`. Never fold it into this contract.

A collapsed `[basename, low]` fan-out line (one summary line counting many matches, e.g. `src/messages/en/research.json: 88 test files match [basename, low] — e.g. … — too generic to enumerate`) is **one item**, not 88. Treat it as generic-basename noise: the basename matched incidentally, not because the tests exercise the entry. Do not enumerate or classify the sampled paths individually; grep-verify only if the entry is plausibly affected by the contract's change.

An `unverified` confidence tag means derivation found no hit (default export, indirect reference, or no affected tests). Confirm by reading the test files or declare known paths directly in `files` — never assume `unverified` means "no tests affected".

## Rules

- Behaviors that carry the business rules are testable. Scaffolding, scripts, and config are manual.
- Declare superseded and obsolete test paths in `files`. Undeclared test paths are protected by the staged-diff guard: deleting or skipping them halts implementation.
- Set `status: "active"` for all behaviors in the contract.
- Be specific. Vague `expectedOutput` cannot be tested.
- Advisory warnings never block the save, but read every one — each names a contract-quality issue you can fix before `/implement`.

arguments.instruction:
Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step below is one green commit, in order.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. This minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden (golden vectors stay owned by internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go; see decision below).

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain` — one step per docs/api contract file in the order documented in docs/api/AGENTS.md. The 10 chain values (partyId, adminJwt, bootstrapToken, globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId, paymentId, accessToken, webhookId, listingCount) become Extract -> Vars. No setNextRequest involvement.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. Add FLOW_GATEWAY_URL (plus admin credential env vars) so the harness skips launchGateway and targets an external gateway. scripts/payment-capture.sh runs it and keeps reading the DRILL_PAYMENT_URL= marker from stdout; mise run payment works as before.

5. ATOMIC cutover (single commit): strip bru.runner.setNextRequest and chain bru.setVar/getVar from every docs/api/*.yml; move cross-request assertions (list-parties, party-detail, audit-events, get-listings, resolve-identity, mint-approval) to declared inputs or ExpectFn; runtime {{process.env.x}} -> {{x}} (static config may keep process.env); drillMode stays an input; delete scripts/bru-run.sh and scripts/bru-drill.sh; remove JWT minting and party key generation from scripts/provide-test-environment.sh (it keeps gateway env + operator credentials + gateway signing keys); replace qc.sh --api/--e2e with --flow (GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -v, no -run filter); update .mise.toml qc description; rewrite the Chaining and QC Chain sections of docs/api/AGENTS.md to describe inputs and point to docs/flows/.

6. Route auth matrix. Add auth class tags to info.tags in all 41 docs/api/*.yml (auth:admin, auth:party, auth:ticket, auth:provider, auth:public). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists every file, asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public route, and fails if any file lacks an auth tag.

7. Standing tests under one entry: --flow runs ./internal/app/integration/... with no -run filter so payload_bytes_test.go, plaintext_pii_test.go and ticket_verification_test.go (ungated, package integration) run in both --test and --flow; gateway-backed tests stay gated by GATEWAY_E2E=1. Fold any test-file renames/updates into this behavior.

8. Narrative guides docs/flows/onboarding.md, docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md, docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md, docs/flows/payment.md: prose sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to its docs/api file.

Decision (Q5, minter ownership): keep the two minters separate. Golden vectors keep their committed-key, fixed-timestamp signing path owned by webhooks/golden_test.go (byte-pinned, guarded by TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey). The flow harness minter lives in e2e, generates a fresh key per run, and mints live iat/exp/jti. Both consume shared claim/typ constants from pkg/jwttyp and production code; no new shared pkg/ minter.

Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step below is one green commit, in order.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. This minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden (golden vectors stay owned by internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go; see decision below).

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain` — one step per docs/api contract file in the order documented in docs/api/AGENTS.md. The 10 chain values (partyId, adminJwt, bootstrapToken, globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId, paymentId, accessToken, webhookId, listingCount) become Extract -> Vars. No setNextRequest involvement.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. Add FLOW_GATEWAY_URL (plus admin credential env vars) so the harness skips launchGateway and targets an external gateway; keep TestMain/shutdownSuite teardown working whether or not the gateway was launched. scripts/payment-capture.sh runs it and keeps reading the DRILL_PAYMENT_URL= marker from stdout; mise run payment works as before.

5. ATOMIC cutover (single commit): strip bru.runner.setNextRequest and chain bru.setVar/getVar from every docs/api/*.yml; move cross-request assertions (list-parties, party-detail, audit-events, get-listings, resolve-identity, mint-approval) to declared inputs or ExpectFn; runtime {{process.env.x}} -> {{x}} (static config may keep process.env); drillMode stays an input; delete scripts/bru-run.sh and scripts/bru-drill.sh; remove JWT minting and party key generation from scripts/provide-test-environment.sh (it keeps gateway env + operator credentials + gateway signing keys); replace qc.sh --api/--e2e with --flow (GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -v, no -run filter); update .mise.toml qc description; update .github/workflows/pr-check.yml (replace qc --api + raw e2e go test with mise run qc --flow) and e2e-nightly.yml (use mise run qc --flow); rewrite the Chaining and QC Chain sections of docs/api/AGENTS.md to describe inputs and point to docs/flows/.

6. Route auth matrix. Add auth class tags to info.tags in all 41 docs/api/*.yml (auth:admin, auth:party, auth:ticket, auth:provider, auth:public). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists every file, asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public route, and fails if any file lacks an auth tag.

7. Standing tests under one entry: --flow runs ./internal/app/integration/... with no -run filter so payload_bytes_test.go, plaintext_pii_test.go and ticket_verification_test.go (ungated, package integration) run in both --test and --flow; gateway-backed tests stay gated by GATEWAY_E2E=1. Fold any test-file renames/updates into this behavior.

8. Narrative guides docs/flows/onboarding.md, docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md, docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md, docs/flows/payment.md: prose sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to its docs/api file. These four files are new (created by this step).

Decision (Q5, minter ownership): keep the two minters separate. Golden vectors keep their committed-key, fixed-timestamp signing path owned by webhooks/golden_test.go (byte-pinned, guarded by TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey). The flow harness minter lives in e2e, generates a fresh key per run, and mints live iat/exp/jti. Both consume shared claim/typ constants from pkg/jwttyp and production code; no new shared pkg/ minter.

task.title: Plan 018: Flow harness with single opt-in `--flow` entry
task.instruction:
Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step below is one green commit, in order.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. This minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden (golden vectors stay owned by internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go; see decision below).

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain` — one step per docs/api contract file in the order documented in docs/api/AGENTS.md. The 10 chain values (partyId, adminJwt, bootstrapToken, globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId, paymentId, accessToken, webhookId, listingCount) become Extract -> Vars. No setNextRequest involvement.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. Add FLOW_GATEWAY_URL (plus admin credential env vars) so the harness skips launchGateway and targets an external gateway; keep TestMain/shutdownSuite teardown working whether or not the gateway was launched. scripts/payment-capture.sh runs it and keeps reading the DRILL_PAYMENT_URL= marker from stdout; mise run payment works as before.

5. ATOMIC cutover (single commit): strip bru.runner.setNextRequest and chain bru.setVar/getVar from every docs/api/*.yml; move cross-request assertions (list-parties, party-detail, audit-events, get-listings, resolve-identity, mint-approval) to declared inputs or ExpectFn; runtime {{process.env.x}} -> {{x}} (static config may keep process.env); drillMode stays an input; delete scripts/bru-run.sh and scripts/bru-drill.sh; remove JWT minting and party key generation from scripts/provide-test-environment.sh (it keeps gateway env + operator credentials + gateway signing keys); replace qc.sh --api/--e2e with --flow (GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -v, no -run filter); update .mise.toml qc description; update .github/workflows/pr-check.yml (replace qc --api + raw e2e go test with mise run qc --flow) and e2e-nightly.yml (use mise run qc --flow); rewrite the Chaining and QC Chain sections of docs/api/AGENTS.md to describe inputs and point to docs/flows/.

6. Route auth matrix. Add auth class tags to info.tags in all 41 docs/api/*.yml (auth:admin, auth:party, auth:ticket, auth:provider, auth:public). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists every file, asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public route, and fails if any file lacks an auth tag.

7. Standing tests under one entry: --flow runs ./internal/app/integration/... with no -run filter so payload_bytes_test.go, plaintext_pii_test.go and ticket_verification_test.go (ungated, package integration) run in both --test and --flow; gateway-backed tests stay gated by GATEWAY_E2E=1. Fold any test-file renames/updates into this behavior.

8. Narrative guides docs/flows/onboarding.md, docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md, docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md, docs/flows/payment.md: prose sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to its docs/api file. These four files are new (created by this step).

Decision (Q5, minter ownership): keep the two minters separate. Golden vectors keep their committed-key, fixed-timestamp signing path owned by webhooks/golden_test.go (byte-pinned, guarded by TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey). The flow harness minter lives in e2e, generates a fresh key per run, and mints live iat/exp/jti. Both consume shared claim/typ constants from pkg/jwttyp and production code; no new shared pkg/ minter.

task.title: Plan 018: Flow harness with single opt-in `--flow` entry
task.instruction:
Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step below is one green commit, in order.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. This minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden (golden vectors stay owned by internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go; see decision below).

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain` — one step per docs/api contract file in the order documented in docs/api/AGENTS.md. The 10 chain values (partyId, adminJwt, bootstrapToken, globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId, paymentId, accessToken, webhookId, listingCount) become Extract -> Vars. No setNextRequest involvement.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. Add FLOW_GATEWAY_URL (plus admin credential env vars) so the harness skips launchGateway and targets an external gateway; keep TestMain/shutdownSuite teardown working whether or not the gateway was launched. scripts/payment-capture.sh runs it and keeps reading the DRILL_PAYMENT_URL= marker from stdout; mise run payment works as before.

5. ATOMIC cutover (single commit): strip bru.runner.setNextRequest and chain bru.setVar/getVar from every docs/api/*.yml; move cross-request assertions (list-parties, party-detail, audit-events, get-listings, resolve-identity, mint-approval) to declared inputs or ExpectFn; runtime {{process.env.x}} -> {{x}} (static config may keep process.env); drillMode stays an input; delete scripts/bru-run.sh and scripts/bru-drill.sh; remove JWT minting and party key generation from scripts/provide-test-environment.sh (it keeps gateway env + operator credentials + gateway signing keys); replace qc.sh --api/--e2e with --flow (GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -v, no -run filter); update .mise.toml qc description; update .github/workflows/pr-check.yml (replace qc --api + raw e2e go test with mise run qc --flow) and e2e-nightly.yml (use mise run qc --flow); rewrite the Chaining and QC Chain sections of docs/api/AGENTS.md to describe inputs and point to docs/flows/.

6. Route auth matrix. Add auth class tags to info.tags in all 41 docs/api/*.yml (auth:admin, auth:party, auth:ticket, auth:provider, auth:public). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists every file, asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public route, and fails if any file lacks an auth tag.

7. Standing tests under one entry: --flow runs ./internal/app/integration/... with no -run filter so payload_bytes_test.go, plaintext_pii_test.go and ticket_verification_test.go (ungated, package integration) run in both --test and --flow; gateway-backed tests stay gated by GATEWAY_E2E=1. Fold any test-file renames/updates into this behavior.

8. Narrative guides docs/flows/onboarding.md, docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md, docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md, docs/flows/payment.md: prose sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to its docs/api file. These four files are new (created by this step).

Decision (Q5, minter ownership): keep the two minters separate. Golden vectors keep their committed-key, fixed-timestamp signing path owned by webhooks/golden_test.go (byte-pinned, guarded by TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey). The flow harness minter lives in e2e, generates a fresh key per run, and mints live iat/exp/jti. Both consume shared claim/typ constants from pkg/jwttyp and production code; no new shared pkg/ minter.
