task.title: Plan 018: Flow harness with single opt-in `--flow` entry
task.instruction:
Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step below is one green commit, in order.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. This minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden (golden vectors stay owned by internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go; see decision below).

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain` — one step per docs/api contract file in the order documented in docs/api/AGENTS.md. The 10 chain values (partyId, adminJwt, bootstrapToken, globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId, paymentId, accessToken, webhookId, listingCount) become Extract -> Vars. No setNextRequest involvement.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. Add FLOW_GATEWAY_URL (plus admin credential env vars) so the harness skips launchGateway and targets an external gateway; keep TestMain/shutdownSuite teardown working whether or not the gateway was launched. scripts/payment-capture.sh runs it and keeps reading the DRILL_PAYMENT_URL= marker from stdout; mise run payment works as before.

5. ATOMIC cutover (single commit): strip bru.runner.setNextRequest and chain bru.setVar/getVar from every docs/api/*.yml; move cross-request assertions (list-parties, party-detail, audit-events, get-listings, resolve-identity, mint-approval) to declared inputs or ExpectFn; runtime {{process.env.x}} -> {{x}} (static config may keep process.env); drillMode stays an input; delete scripts/bru-run.sh and scripts/bru-drill.sh; remove JWT minting and party key generation from scripts/provide-test-environment.sh (it keeps gateway env + operator credentials + gateway signing keys); replace qc.sh --api/--e2e with --flow (GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/... -v, no -run filter); update .mise.toml qc description; update .github/workflows/pr-check.yml (replace qc --api + raw e2e go test with mise run qc --flow) and e2e-nightly.yml (use mise run qc --flow); rewrite the Chaining and QC Chain sections of docs/api/AGENTS.md to describe inputs and point to docs/flows/.

6. Route auth matrix. Add auth class tags to info.tags in all 41 docs/api/*.yml (auth:admin, auth:party, auth:ticket, auth:provider, auth:public). Scenario `FlowRouteAuthMatrix` lists every file, asserts 401 with no credential for each non-public route, and fails if any file lacks an auth tag.

7. Standing tests under one entry: --flow runs ./internal/app/integration/... with no -run filter so payload_bytes_test.go, plaintext_pii_test.go and ticket_verification_test.go (ungated, package integration) run in both --test and --flow; gateway-backed tests stay gated by GATEWAY_E2E=1. Fold any test-file renames/updates into this behavior.

8. Narrative guides docs/flows/onboarding.md, docs/flows/approval-direct-exchange.md, docs/flows/webhook-delivery.md, docs/flows/payment.md: prose sequence, who signs what, which key verifies it, each step linking to its docs/api file. These four files are new (created by this step).

Decision (Q5, minter ownership): keep the two minters separate. Golden vectors keep their committed-key, fixed-timestamp signing path owned by webhooks/golden_test.go (byte-pinned, guarded by TestGolden_NoProdCodeLoadsTestKey). The flow harness minter lives in e2e, generates a fresh key per run, and mints live iat/exp/jti. Both consume shared claim/typ constants from pkg/jwttyp and production code; no new shared pkg/ minter.

content.text:
Splitting T3 so each commit lands green quickly, before the deep read of all 28 files.

## T3 as 4 commits

**T3a — Chain plumbing (the risky core).** ~6 steps in documented order, enough to prove `Extract → Vars` works end to end: `health`, `admin/login`, `admin/create-bootstrap-token`, `parties/register-party`, `parties/promote-party`, `parties/party-health`. This is where the earlier timeouts clustered. It resolves the open question from the last runs — whether `bru run` writes a parseable report when an after-response script throws. The chain files carry `setNextRequest`/`setVar`; in single-file runs those should be no-ops, but `parseBruReport` must tolerate a throwing script. Land that fix in this commit.

The values it must carry via `Extract → Vars`: `adminJwt`, `bootstrapToken`, `partyId`. If `party-health` isn't the right 6th file per `docs/api/AGENTS.md` order, substitute the actual next file — the point is one scenario that crosses the register→promote→read boundary.

**T3b — Marketplace/approval leg.** The listing/approval steps, carrying `globalKey`, `approvalTicket`, `listingId`.

**T3c — Invocation/webhook leg.** Carrying `accessToken`, `webhookId`, `listingCount`.

**T3d — Payments leg.** Carrying `paymentId`. Note: `payments/create-payment` has a drill-mode early stop, so this leg must pass `drillMode=0` (or the non-drill input) explicitly. If T4 (`FlowPaymentDrill`) is easier to land before this, do that and reuse the input wiring — tell me if you'd rather reorder to T4 before T3d.

The 10 chain values are named in the contract, so the split preserves the DoD: `FlowQCChain` still covers all 28 calls when T3d lands; T3a–T3c are just intermediate green states.

## Getting the rest done

The halts were all exploration overrunning the 600s window before code landed. Two rules to fix that:

1. **Read in the same commit's budget, not before it.** For each commit, read only the contract files that commit runs (T3a reads 6 files, not all 28). The full-chain ordering from `docs/api/AGENTS.md` gets read once, in T3a, and pinned as a Go table — then T3b–T3d just extend the table.
2. **Land a skeleton before the deep read.** If a step needs a new helper (e.g. the report-parse tolerance), commit the helper + one passing step first, then extend.

After T3, the remaining behaviors in order, each one commit:

- **T4** — `FlowPaymentDrill`, `FLOW_GATEWAY_URL` external-gateway skip, `payment-capture.sh` marker, teardown intact.
- **T5** — atomic cutover (must be one commit: strip chain logic from `docs/api` only after `FlowQCChain` covers it; delete `bru-run.sh`/`bru-drill.sh`; `--flow` in `qc.sh`/`.mise.toml`/both workflows; `docs/api/AGENTS.md`). Depends on T3 + T4 being green, since it removes the shell path.
- **T6** — `auth:*` tags on 41 files + `FlowRouteAuthMatrix`.
- **T7** — standing tests under `--flow` (mostly falls out of the `--flow` definition in T5; this commit is verification + any test-file adjustment).
- **T8** — `docs/flows/*.md`, docs only.

Nothing I can do from here — this is discussion only. To proceed: re-run `/finalize` to rewrite the contract with the T3a–T3d split (I'll draft the revised behaviors), or just `/implement` to resume T3 as a single unit again. Which do you want?

# Finalize the Task Contract

You are drafting the atomic implementation contract from this discussion.

## Steps

1. Derive the task from the chat history. The conversation is the source of truth.
2. Draft the contract and call `save_task` with all fields.
3. `save_task` returns deterministic scan evidence and advisory warnings. Classify each evidence item (see Test classification) and revise the contract if the evidence surfaces test paths you missed. You may read files to confirm a specific fact — an exact path, an existing signature, or an `unverified` evidence item — but the discussion stays the primary source.
4. Call `save_task` again with the revised contract. Iterate until the evidence and warnings are clean or consciously accepted.

## Fields

- `title` — short task name.
- `instruction` — what to implement.
- `files` — files affected. Declare every test path the contract updates or removes here (see Test classification).
- `done` — definition of done (manual verification for non-test work).
- `behaviors[]` — each behavior: `id`, `description`, `expectedOutput`, `kind`, `status`, optional `sourceFile`.

## Co-location rule (atomic green commits)

**One behavior = test + implementation in the same commit — never split.**

- `kind: "test"` means *verified-by-test*: the behavior carries the observable outcome AND the test that verifies it. The commit lands green because test and implementation ship together.
- A behavior whose `expectedOutput` describes test artifacts only ("test file contains 3 cases", "tests covering edge cases") is invalid: such a commit is **red by construction** — a test without its implementation. Rewrite the `expectedOutput` as the observable behavior the test asserts.
- Behaviors must be **independently green-committable**: each behavior's commit passes the project's pre-commit hooks on its own. No test-before-implementation splits, no scaffold-only behaviors.
- Test updates never form their own behavior. When a behavior supersedes or removes existing tests, fold the test change into that same behavior's `instruction` and commit.

## Test classification

`save_task` returns **scan evidence**: per-`files`-entry match lines with method and confidence tags (`[symbol, high]`, `[basename, low]`, `unverified`), plus advisory warnings (`undeclared-referencing`, `declared-not-found`, `no-evidence`). Classify every evidence item:

- **preserved** — the test asserts behavior the contract keeps. Do not declare it; the guard protects it automatically.
- **superseded** — the test asserts old behavior the contract changes. Declare the path in `files`, and describe the required test update in the superseding behavior's `instruction` (folded, never its own behavior).
- **obsolete** — the test covers behavior the contract removes. Declare the path in `files`; for pure-removal contracts describe the removal in a manual behavior ("remove legacy path + its tests; suite green").
- **out-of-scope** — the test is already dead or broken for reasons unrelated to this contract. Report it to the user as a recommendation for a separate `/discuss`. Never fold it into this contract.

A collapsed `[basename, low]` fan-out line (one summary line counting many matches, e.g. `src/messages/en/research.json: 88 test files match [basename, low] — e.g. … — too generic to enumerate`) is **one item**, not 88. Treat it as generic-basename noise: the basename matched incidentally, not because the tests exercise the entry. Do not enumerate or classify the sampled paths individually; grep-verify only if the entry is plausibly affected by the contract's change.

An `unverified` confidence tag means derivation found no hit (default export, indirect reference, or no affected tests). Confirm by reading the test files or declare known paths directly in `files` — never assume `unverified` means "no tests affected".

## Rules

- Behaviors that carry the business rules are testable. Scaffolding, scripts, and config are manual.
- Declare superseded and obsolete test paths in `files`. Undeclared test paths are protected by the staged-diff guard: deleting or skipping them halts implementation.
- Set `status: "active"` for all behaviors in the contract.
- Be specific. Vague `expectedOutput` cannot be tested.
- Advisory warnings never block the save, but read every one — each names a contract-quality issue you can fix before `/implement`.
Drafting the revised contract with the T3a–T3d split and the resume-state fixes.

task.instruction:
Implement Plan 018 (docs/plans/018-flow-harness.md): consolidate the two test drivers (shell `bru-run.sh` chain and the `e2e` Go harness) into one opt-in flow harness while keeping `docs/api` pure contract. Keep the existing `e2e` package (do NOT rename). Each numbered step is one green commit, in order.

Execution rules (adopted after three 600s halts during exploration):
- Read only the contract files the current commit runs; do not front-load reads of all 28 files.
- Pin the full 28-file order from docs/api/AGENTS.md as a Go table in T3a, then extend the table in T3b-T3d without re-reading.
- Land skeleton + first passing step before any deep read; commit early, extend after.

1. Add `ExpectFn func(body []byte, vars map[string]string) error` to `Step` in internal/app/integration/e2e/scenario.go for body-level assertions bru 4.2.0 cannot express. `runScenarios` invokes it after `Expect`. Existing e2e scenarios (marketplace, invocation, payments, result_switch) pass unchanged.

2. Party lifecycle + driver minter. Extend internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures.go so a `party` helper generates an Ed25519 key in memory, enrolls through the register-party contract file, reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via Extract, and mints party tokens in Go (iss = party_id). Add negative-token options from the same minter: forged signature, foreign key, past iat/exp, wrong typ, wrong aud, wrong iss. Minter stays test-side in e2e; do NOT create a shared pkg/ minter and do NOT touch testdata/golden.

3. Port the 28-call QC chain as scenario `FlowQCChain`, split into four independently green commits. T3a pins the full 28-file order (from docs/api/AGENTS.md) as a Go scenario table and lands the first ~6 steps in documented order (health, admin login, create-bootstrap-token, register-party, promote-party, then the next documented file), carrying adminJwt, bootstrapToken, partyId via Extract -> Vars; it also makes parseBruReport tolerate a report produced when an after-response script throws (chain files carry setNextRequest/setVar, no-ops in single-file runs). T3b adds the marketplace/approval leg, carrying globalKey, approvalTicket, listingId. T3c adds the invocation/webhook leg, carrying accessToken, webhookId, listingCount. T3d adds the payments leg, carrying paymentId, passing the non-drill input explicitly (create-payment has a drill-mode early stop). No setNextRequest involvement in any leg. The full FlowQCChain covers all 28 calls when T3d lands.

4. Port the payment drill as scenario `FlowPaymentDrill` with drillMode=1 as a step input. data.text: The prior commit `8ee2e90` already implemented T2's minter. Let me verify it compiles and check the current state more carefully.
T2 was already landed in commit `8ee2e90`. Let me verify the current state compiles, the tests pass, and the invariants (minter test-side, golden untouched) hold.
The T2 implementation already landed in commit `8ee2e90`. Now let me verify it's actually green against a live gateway (GATEWAY_E2E=1).
All T2 fixture tests pass against a live gateway. Now verify the existing scenarios still pass and the whole repo is green.

T2 was already landed in commit `8ee2e90 test(e2e): mint party tokens in Go with negative variants`. My verification confirms the behavior is complete and green; no further changes were needed.

**What the landed behavior contains** (all in `internal/app/integration/e2e/`):

- **`minter.go`** (new, test-side): `partyFixture` generates a per-run Ed25519 keypair with a unique kid; `enrollParty` in `fixtures.go` registers through `docs/api/parties/register-party.yml` and reads the server-assigned `party_id` from the bru report via `extractJSONPath` (the same Extract path the scenario runner uses); `mintJWT` stamps `iss = PartyID` with live iat/exp and fresh jti. Negative options from the same minter: `withForgedSignature`, `withForeignKey`, `withPastIatExp`, `withTyp`, `withAud`, `withIss`.
- **`fixtures_test.go`**: `TestFixturesEnrollMintsIssPartyID` asserts the minted token's `iss` equals the registered `party_id` and authenticates; `TestFixturesNegativeTokens` asserts forged signature / foreign key / past iat-exp yield 401 against the live gateway, and pins that wrong typ/aud/iss pass today (PartyAuth only checks kid+signature+exp — the claim tightening belongs to plans 019–022).

**Verification performed:**
- `GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/e2e/ -run TestFixtures -v` — all 5 fixture tests plus all 6 negative subtests PASS against a freshly booted gateway.
- `GATEWAY_E2E=1 go test ./internal/app/integration/...` — full suite green (87s), so existing marketplace/invocation/payments/result_switch scenarios are unaffected.
- `go test ./...` — green.
- Invariants confirmed: no shared pkg/ minter (minter lives in the e2e package), `internal/app/services/webhooks/golden_test.go` and `testdata/golden` last touched by pre-plan commits (`5ee5c05`, `72ca082`), untouched by the T2 commit.

```json
{
  "summary": "T2 (party lifecycle + Go minter with negative variants) was already landed in commit 8ee2e90; verified green end to end: enrollParty registers through the bru contract file, reads server-assigned party_id via Extract, mints iss=party_id tokens, and all six negative variants behave as pinned (401 for forged/foreign/expired, 200 boundary for wrong typ/aud/iss). Full GATEWAY_E2E=1 integration suite and go test ./... pass; minter stays test-side in e2e, golden_test.go and testdata/golden untouched.",
  "suggestedCommit": "test(e2e): mint party tokens in Go with negative variants"
}
```

The T2 implementation appears to already be committed (8ee2e90). Let me verify the remaining gaps against the expected output — specifically the scenario-side minting path and any ungated minter coverage.

The T2 implementation is already committed (8ee2e90), but every T2 test is gateway-gated (`GATEWAY_E2E=1`), so with the suite gate off the minter has zero coverage — nothing pins that each negative variant actually carries its forged attribute, or that `mintIntoVars` adopts the extracted party id as `iss`. I'll land that missing ungated coverage in the declared file `fixtures_test.go` (red-first against the variant structure).

All green: new ungated tests pass, `go vet` clean, full `./internal/app/integration/...` passes without the gateway gate, and only the declared file `internal/app/integration/e2e/fixtures_test.go` is modified (216 lines, under the 300 limit; `webhooks/golden_test.go` and `testdata/golden` untouched).

What landed for T2's retry: the minter implementation was already committed (8ee2e90), but every T2 assertion was gateway-gated, so nothing pinned the negative-variant structure or the `mintIntoVars` plumbing under the ungated suite entry. The two new tests close that gap:

- `TestMinterNegativeVariants` — parses each variant from the same e2e minter and asserts the forged attribute: control token carries the registered kid with `iss` = party id; forged signature keeps the kid; foreign key presents an unregistered kid; past iat/exp is expired on arrival; wrong typ/aud/iss stamp the header/claims.
- `TestMintIntoVars` — the Pre hook adopts the party id extracted from the bru report and mints with `iss` = that id; minting before extraction fails instead of inventing an issuer.

Both pass without GATEWAY_E2E, as does the full integration package and go vet; webhooks/golden_test.go and testdata/golden are untouched.",

```json
}
```
